title: Knothe-Rosenblatt Quantile Regression for Risk-sensitive Multi-objective Reinforcement Learning
claim: Prior approaches fail to preserve the structure of a multivariate distribution when mapping particles between domain and codomain; ours reproduces it faithfully.
layout: 4 boxed columns left-to-right, domain over codomain, color-coded borders per method
description: Four boxed columns, each with a color gradient square (the domain) on top and a downward arrow to a 2-D point cloud (the codomain) below. The first column, in black, is the ground truth. It shows a smooth spiral curve, with a color legend for Value 1 (red) and Value 2 (blue) and axis labels. The next three columns are the Marginal (purple), MMD (orange) and KR-map (ours, blue) methods. The Marginal method fills the square with a blocky, scattered cloud. MMD gives a distorted spiral with crossing gray lines that link the corner suit symbols (diamond, heart, spade, club) to their images. KR-map recovers a clean spiral with nearly straight corner links. The eye goes first to the colorful gradients, then to the bottom row, where the spiral shapes differ.

abstract: In this work, we extend distributional reinforcement learning (RL) to develop a risk-sensitive multi-objective RL framework, with applications to domains such as finance and robotics. We achieve this by adopting vector-risk measures and approximating them via Knothe-Rosenblatt (KR) quantile regression. This approach directly extends the IQN framework to the multi-objective setting, aligns with the axiomatic definition of vector-risk measures, and guarantees that critics converge under the distributional Bellman operator. To mitigate the artificial ordering imposed by the KR map, we employ a transformer architecture without positional encoding, and introduce MO-TQC for training stability. We demonstrate improved performance on MO-Gymnasium benchmarks and use our framework to study risk-sensitive policies in multi-objective tasks.
